summary: Assign the existing 83/91 example to the person-as-victim construction 1c.

summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC NE Ditin Hazar/37)

data.turoyo: Hedik̇a i+žǝnk̇e… i+k̇ačk̇este mašəkla, Diṫə́n Hăzár mašəkla d̥koməgnu u+medayḏa. Lo+damixo.
data.translation: Then the woman… the girl also noticed, Seeing Nightingale noticed that her stuff (lit. ‘her thing’) is getting stolen. (So) she didn’t go to sleep.

summary: New box ko-Preterit: example for sense 1 in ko-Preterit (95/147)

summary: New sense 1b: (mit Personenobjekt) entführen, einen Menschen wegnehmen und fortbringen

data.label: 1b
data.gloss: (mit Personenobjekt) entführen, einen Menschen wegnehmen und fortbringen

rationale: PrS 42/54 combines a human object with mamṭatle l gabi, explicitly transporting that person. JTM 5.3 repeatedly identifies intended abduction, whereas existing 83/91 concerns robbing a person's property. The contrast is in the event, not just animacy.

summary: New sense 1c: (mit Personenobjekt) j-n bestehlen, berauben
rationale: The existing 83/91 example has a person object but stolen clothing, not transportation of that person. Make the dispossessed-person construction explicit without rewriting sense 1.

data.turoyo: Əzzənwo hənne b lalyo gunwiwunne əšmo d suġle du daḥno, w uṯanwo mdaqdəqiwole saymiwole laḥmo, b gnowo, d lo maṭ ṭaye.

summary: example for sense 1b in Infectum (JTM 5.3/12)

data.turoyo: <...> mərre ašər kit harke barṯo d malko, kətle tloṯ abnoṯo, ksaymina lə ksaymina lə qqudrina gunwinalle.
data.translation: Sie sagten: Es gibt hier eine Königstochter ... (Der König) hat drei Töchter. So sehr wir uns auch anstrengen, wir können sie nicht entführen.

summary: example for sense 1b in Infinitiv (JTM 5.3/29)

data.turoyo: omər maḥkəlalli i masale d barṯux, d koṯən lu gnowo w lə qqudri gunwila.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part act. (MAC Ishaq old houses/89)

data.turoyo: Meqəm kətwa ganowe, kətwa ḥăramiye. Lo? Ganowe, gunwiwa aʕ+ʕənwe, gunwiwa ann+afšoṯe, kummínanne, kuḏʕitu ann+afšoṯe, lo? Ann+afšoṯe, ak+karme.
data.translation: Formerly there were thieves, there were robbers, right? Thieves, they stole grapes, they stole raisins, we call them, you know raisins, right? Raisins, vineyards.

rationale: Supplies sentence context for the inherited bare Part act. ganowo and an agentive plural; one quotation covers the repeated nominal token.

summary: New idiom: b-gnowo 'heimlich, verstohlen'

data.turoyo: Qayəm u dewo, mədle li tfangayḏe w aṯi b gnowo.
data.translation: Unterdessen machte sich der Wolf auf, ergriff ein Gewehr und kam heimlich heran

rationale: No theft occurs in the approach clause. Same manner phrase in JTM 3.2/29 and PrS 85/80. Permitted gnowo search finds the phrase in ṭʕn 1 examples, not a separately listed idiom; register it here once.

summary: Objects distinguish three roles: stolen property, transported human abductee, and human dispossessed victim. Animate reference alone is insufficient: PrS 42/54 and 83/91 have different event structures.

The inherited Detransitive Infinitiv box contains gnowo with active event meaning. Its location is preserved as editorial practice, not taken as proof of agent suppression. b-gnowo additionally has a manner use independent of theft.
ganowo is filed as Part act. in the entry, although ganowe in these narratives are lexicalized agent nouns. One contextual plural example is added without asserting an ongoing event.

New Detransitive Infectum məgnu contrasts with result-state gniwe and the existing Detransitive Preterit gniw. Active gniwənne/gniwile spellings warrant dialectal analysis; neither is silently forced into the Detransitive.

The PrS numbers of identical inherited quotations differ systematically from those in the supplied reading records. These are possible reference-system differences, not license for automatic citation replacement.
Confirm active gniwənne (MAC Besim History of Bsorino/5) and gniwile (115/9), especially their relationship to the gniw Detransitive base.
Should the inherited Detransitive Infinitiv filing be retained for the active event noun gnowo? It has been preserved pending an editorial decision.
Confirm suffix segmentation in gunwinalle (JTM 5.3/12), associative ganowaṯxu (JL 16.7/30), and gonawnən (PrS 84/7-8).
Resolve PrS text/verse numbers versus the inherited prs page/line references before changing existing citations.
Correct gestolen to gestohlen
rationale: The German past participle of stehlen is gestohlen; the translation is missing h.
